items.stem: On the School Job Assignment page, who assigns staff to temporary jobs?

options.text: The school's principal or their delegate
Any staff member at any school
The HRAD system of record, automatically

items.explanation: It's a self-serve page: the principal — or someone they have delegated — makes the assignments for their own school.

misconceptions.b: This is principal-self-serve, not an IT/Help Desk function.
misconceptions.c: Only the principal or their delegate can assign, and only for their own school's staff.
misconceptions.d: These temporary-job assignments are made by people on the page, not imported automatically.

items.stem: Where do the jobs available on the School Job Assignment page come from?

options.text: Free text typed in by the principal
Whatever jobs HRAD pushes that day
A list the staff member chooses for themselves

items.explanation: Temporary jobs are selected from a canned, predefined list — they aren't entered as free text.

misconceptions.b: Jobs are chosen from a predefined list, not typed freely.
misconceptions.c: The list is a fixed canned set, not a daily import.
misconceptions.d: The principal or delegate makes the assignment; the staff member doesn't pick their own job here.

items.stem: Whose staff can a principal assign on the School Job Assignment page?

options.text: Staff at any school in their municipal division

items.explanation: The page is school-scoped: a principal assigns staff at their own school. District-wide assignment is a separate page (S3.9).

misconceptions.b: District-wide assignment is the separate Temporary Job Assignment page (S3.9), not this one.
misconceptions.c: The scope is the principal's own school, not a wider geographic grouping.
misconceptions.d: It covers the school's staff, not a specific worker category only.

items.stem: A principal needs a short-term role filled by a teacher at their own school. Which page is the right self-serve tool, and why?

options.text: School Job Assignment — it's school-scoped and the principal (or delegate) assigns their own staff to a temporary job from the canned list
The district-wide Temporary Job Assignment page (S3.9), because all temporary jobs are assigned district-wide
The Schools page, by adding a new job field to the school record
A Help Desk ticket, since principals can't assign jobs themselves

items.explanation: For a temporary job at the principal's own school, School Job Assignment is the school-scoped, principal-self-serve page; the job is picked from the canned list.

misconceptions.b: S3.9 is district-wide; a single-school need is handled on the school-scoped page.
misconceptions.c: Job assignments aren't done by editing the school record on the Schools page.
misconceptions.d: Principals (or delegates) self-serve here — no Help Desk ticket is required.

items.stem: In one or two sentences, describe what the School Job Assignment page does and how it differs from the district-wide Temporary Job Assignment page (S3.9).
rubric: States principals or their delegates assign staff at their own school to temporary jobs
Notes the jobs come from a canned/predefined list
Contrasts the school scope here with the district-wide scope of S3.9
items.sampleAnswer: On the School Job Assignment page a principal (or their delegate) assigns staff at their own school to temporary jobs chosen from a canned list. It's school-scoped, unlike the district-wide Temporary Job Assignment page (S3.9), which assigns across the whole district.
